item.title: German business confidence rises in October despite global economic risks
item.description: Germany's ifo Business Climate Index rose in October, driven by stronger manufacturing confidence, although higher energy prices and interest rates continue to pose risks to the economic recovery.

item.title: Ebola: Uganda restricts travel as Nigerian case evacuated to Europe
item.description: The Ebola outbreak that began in the Democratic Republic of Congo in May, now the fastest-growing and most widespread on record, has caused nearly 10,000 confirmed cases across Africa.

item.title: Dictionary.com reveals 2026 Word of the Year - and it's a depressing one
item.description: The internet slang term / suffix "Maxxing" has officially been selected by Dictionary.com as its 2026 Word of the Year.

item.title: Claude bypassed paywall to access US election data without being asked, days before midterms
item.description: The incident is the latest in a string this year that has raised concerns over Big Tech’s ability to maintain control of its increasingly autonomous AI models and curb their rogue behaviour.

item.title: New business projects decline despite rising foreign investment, UN says at World Investment Forum in Doha
item.description: Foreign investment is rising, but fewer new projects are being announced and funding remains concentrated in a few economies. At the World Investment Forum in Doha, officials and investors are discussing how more countries can benefit and create jobs.

item.title: Algeria approves troop deployment to Niger: what is their mission?
item.description: This rare move comes amid strengthened security ties between Algeria and Niamey following the thwarting of an attempted coup in Niger in August.

item.title: Airbnb changed its check-out chore rules – and hosts are fuming about it
item.description: Some are calling for a boycott of the short-term rental platform after hosts were banned from asking guests to strip bed linens or do the washing up.

item.title: Yeast or famine: Australian convicted murderer loses bid to eat Vegemite in prison
item.description: A convicted murderer has lost a legal bid to overturn a ban on Vegemite in Victoria's prisons, despite his claims that the ban was unlawful because it denied him his human right to enjoy Australian culture.

item.title: Japanese company to compensate users hit by cyberattack
item.description: GMO Internet, a Japanese internet infrastructure company, will compensate customers for losses from unauthorised trading linked to a cyberattack on its cloud service, and will make a ¥5,000 (€28) goodwill payment to every customer currently using the affected service.

item.title: Zelenskyy's planned Brussels visit for peace talks cancelled
item.description: Zelenskyy said the planned visit would gather Ukraine, the US, EU and NATO in high-level talks on security guarantees and diplomatic efforts to end Russia's war against Ukraine.

item.title: Galp and Moeve fail to agree merger of refining and distribution operations
item.description: Portuguese multinational energy corporation Galp confirmed that talks with shareholders of major Spanish energy firm Moeve, to merge downstream operations, have collapsed, and says the result will not affect its operations.

item.title: Trump officials back Orbán bid for UN secretary-general, WSJ reports
item.description: The WSJ reports that Trump administration officials are floating former Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orbán for UN secretary-general, potentially backed by the US, Russia and China, though nothing is confirmed and his selection remains uncertain.

item.title: Why Israel’s wartime election isn’t just about the battle with Iran and Hamas
item.description: From army exemptions for the ultra-Orthodox to a stalled 7 October inquiry, the issues splitting voters have little to do with Gaza, Lebanon or Iran.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 26th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 26th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Be nice, not nasty: Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton on why AI needs humans at its heart
item.description: Nobel Physics prize winner Geoffrey Hinton is widely regarded as one of the godfathers of artificial intelligence, but he's spent much of the last few years warning against its potential dangers. He discussed those ideas at Starmus and also revealed why 'The Terminator' is his favourite film.

item.title: November 2026 travel guide: Where to go, what to see and the new hotels to book in Europe
item.description: From early Christmas markets in Vienna to late-autumn sunshine in the Canary Islands, November offers plenty of reasons to plan a European escape before the festive rush.

item.title: Revolut to launch platform for investing in private tech companies
item.description: Revolut announced on Monday the launch of Revolut Ventures, a new platform developed with Carne Group to give eligible investors access to private technology companies, an investment market traditionally reserved for wealthy individuals and large institutions.

item.title: 'Pure garbage': Elon Musk’s AI-generated 'The Odyssey' clip ridiculed online
item.description: The AI slop clip has been blasted online, with many calling it out as "garbage" and an "utter waste of time and money like most of Musk Inc."

item.title: One in three young adults use AI chatbots for drug and alcohol information, study finds
item.description: Researchers warn that chatbots could spread misinformation about substance use, as a survey finds that one in three young adults in the United States are turning to AI for drug-related information.

item.title: Oil plunges more than 6% from near wartime highs as diplomacy over Iran seemingly gathers pace
item.description: Brent crude fell more than 6% on Monday morning, retreating from its highest close since March, as regional mediators headed to Tehran and US President Donald Trump weighed a deal with Iran, while investors braced for a week packed with central bank decisions and earnings reports.

item.title: 2.92-metre monster fish: German angler lands giant catfish from Polish reservoir
item.description: Oliver Schäfer from the Eifel and his fishing partner landed a 2.92-metre catfish at a tournament in Poland. The fish is already well known among anglers.

item.title: Mexico: spectacular Catrina parade brings the dead to life
item.description: Skeleton faces, extravagant headdresses and dazzling costumes transformed Mexico City's streets into a colourful spectacle. The annual Catrinas Parade celebrates the country's Day of the Dead traditions.

item.title: Why are Elvis Presley rightsholders suing AI company Anthropic?
item.description: Anthropic could face more than $40million in damages over the alleged unauthorised use of Elvis' music catalogue.

item.title: 'Democracy has won': Europe celebrates Lula's surprise victory in Brazil
item.description: European leaders have greeted Lula's re-election in Brazil. "Democracy and multilateralism have won in Brazil," Ursula von der Leyen said.

item.title: EU hails Serbia’s political upheaval after student group ends Vučić’s rule
item.description: EU leaders and senior officials welcomed the Student List’s election win in Serbia, offering support for reforms and a path to membership after Vučić conceded defeat.

item.title: From metalworker to Brazil's president: Lula da Silva's rise
item.description: Lula broke with his unfavourable record since 1989, winning the runoff after losing the first round, crowning a career that took him from metalworker to Brazil's presidency.

item.title: Lula wins Brazil election after cutting Amazon deforestation to record low
item.description: Lula’s victory in Brazil's presidential election brings hope for the Amazon – but far-right gains threaten progress.

item.title: Ukrainian drone strike on Voronezh kills two as Kyiv and Moscow prepare to restart talks
item.description: Debris from a downed drone hit a moving commuter train, while Zelenskyy says territorial questions must be settled by leaders themselves.

item.title: US: Nicki Minaj endorses Trump at Michigan Republican rally
item.description: Nicki Minaj joined Donald Trump at a Republican rally in Michigan, declaring her support for the president. The event also saw Trump renew his attacks on Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed.

item.title: Can EU Inc still make business easier? Ask the Euronews AI chatbot
item.description: EU Inc, Europe’s harmonised corporate form, is stalled after Parliament’s Committee on Legal Affairs failed to vote. Caught between furious founders and protesting workers, could EU Inc still change how you build a startup? Ask the Euronews AI chatbot.

item.title: Israel is 'on its way become normal again', says former prime minister Ehud Olmert
item.description: Former Israeli prime minister Ehud Olmert believes the country's general election, to be held this Tuesday, is an "inevitable battle about the future of Israel" . He warns the fate of current prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu "may become the disaster of the state Israel".

item.title: 'Extraordinary historical moment' in Serbian democracy, following Vučić defeat
item.description: An "extraordinary historical moment" for Serbian democracy, says top political scientist from the University of Belgrade. Bojan Vranić gives his comments on the recent election results.

item.title: Eric Bauza, the modern voice of Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, dies aged 46
item.description: Prolific voice actor Eric Bauza voiced Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Road Runner and Porky Pig, along with hundreds of other characters.

item.title: EU-Inc: is the EU’s startup booster losing steam? Take our poll.
item.description: With EU-Inc, the EU wanted to help European businesses and startups scale across the entire single market. But loopholes and concerns over worker’s rights keep stalling the initiative.

item.title: Sexy wicker and an Agatha Christie exhibition: The best things to do, hear, see or watch in Europe this week
item.description: Olivia Coleman gets freaky with a wicker husband on the big screen, while London's British Library celebrates the life and works of legendary crime novelist Agatha Christie. Here's what to look out for this week.

item.title: Brazil: Thousands flood streets to celebrate Lula's election victory
item.description: Tears, hugs and dancing filled the streets of Brazil after Lula narrowly defeated Flávio Bolsonaro. Thousands celebrated in Rio and São Paulo as the president secured another four years in office.

item.title: Europe weighs €10bn plan to launch its own astronauts ahead of Rome space summit
item.description: Europe is seeking to boost its presence in space and cut technological dependence on other states. The 15 December ESA summit in Rome will shape choices on astronauts, cargo and investment.

item.title: Serbia’s strongman toppled by student-backed movement
item.description: Good morning. It’s Angela Skujins holding the newsletter pen for the entire week. On Monday’s agenda: Serbian elections serve as a death knell for long-time leader Aleksandar Vučić and his political party, while French fury continues to manifest through violent protest and a presidential bid.

item.title: Caught in the act: Italy and Africa join forces against art trafficking
item.description: Cooperation between Italy and Africa is focused on training, traceability and the restoration of cultural heritage.

item.title: Discovering Almaty: Mountain mornings, street art and market flavours
item.description: Kazakhstan’s former capital marked its birthday with music, markets and apple fairs. Beyond the celebrations, mountain breakfasts, colourful architecture and art hiding in plain sight offer reasons to linger.

item.title: ‘It’s improved my life’: Solar kits provide essential power in refugee camps and war zones
item.description: Portable solar kits in disaster zones fuel everything from communication and cooking to cooling and education.

item.title: Europe Today: Serbia’s students topple Vučić as Israel braces for crucial election
item.description: Serbia's student-led movement has secured a historic parliamentary election victory, ending President Aleksandar Vučić's political dominance. Meanwhile, Israel prepares for a crucial election, France faces another wave of mass protests, and Brazil's President Lula wins a fourth term in office.

item.title: Young people's household income in Europe: How does France compare?
item.description: Households with young people aged 18 to 24 generally have lower equivalised disposable income, but experts note that this may not show the full picture.

item.title: Independent republics, castles and bagels: How to spend 24 hours in Vilnius, the capital of Lithuania
item.description: From strolling around the UNESCO-listed Old Town to reading the constitution of the independent republic Užupis, Lithuania’s capital city is perfect to explore in just one day.

item.title: Political earthquake in Serbia: The end of the Vucic Era and the rise of the student list
item.description: This is not simply a change of government. It is the collapse of a political order that has defined Serbia since 2012.

item.title: GPHG 2026: The 'Oscars of watchmaking' scraps gender categories for ‘a breath of fresh air’
item.description: Each year, the world's finest timepieces are celebrated at the Grand Prix d’Horlogerie de Genève (GPHG) award ceremony, which marks its 26th anniversary on Saturday 7 November.

item.title: 'Having money is not enough': Why a job no longer guarantees access to housing in Spain
item.description: House prices rose 84.6% between 2015 and 2025, against 27.85% for average wages. Lack of affordable housing, rent burdens and saving difficulties deepen the crisis as experts call for structural reform.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 26th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 26th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Brazil's Lula clinches election victory as Bolsonaro rejects results
item.description: Lula's triumph bucks a regional trend of victories for right-of-center presidential candidates allied with Trump. It also means Latin America’s largest economy will likely continue defying Trump’s demands, despite the pressure of increased tariffs.

item.title: Serbia: crowds celebrate in Belgrade after Vučić admits defeat
item.description: Crowds celebrated in Belgrade after President Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat for his ruling party in Serbia's snap parliamentary election, following nearly two years of student-led demonstrations.
